description: Framework for classifying content based on AI involvement and human accountability.

levels.name: Fully AI-Generated (Unreviewed)
levels.description: Content generated entirely by AI with no human validation.
levels.note: Not suitable for production or decision-making use.

levels.name: AI-Generated, Human-Reviewed
levels.description: AI-generated content that has been reviewed and validated by a human.
levels.note: Minimum acceptable level for most practical use cases.

levels.name: AI-Assisted, Human-Led
levels.description: Content primarily created by a human with AI providing support (drafting, suggestions, structuring).
levels.note: Default working model for most scenarios.

levels.name: Human-Created, AI-Enhanced
levels.description: Human-created content with minor AI assistance (e.g., grammar, formatting, optimisation).
levels.note: High confidence with minimal AI influence.

levels.name: Fully Human (No AI Involvement)
levels.description: Content created entirely without AI assistance.
levels.note: Used where strict control, compliance, or complete human authorship is required.

principles: AI involvement should be transparent where appropriate
Required level of oversight may vary based on risk and use case

aliases.name: AI-Assisted Reviewed
aliases.description: Officially supported alias of AIG-R representing the same classification level.

classifications: Classification: AICCF: FH (Fully Human - No AI Involvement)

disclaimers: This content was generated with AI assistance and reviewed by a human.
AI-generated output – requires validation before use.
Human-led work supported by AI tools.
This content was created entirely without AI assistance.

alternative.text: This project uses AICCF v1.1 (AI Content Classification Framework) for content classification.

changes: Added official alias AIA-R (AI-Assisted Reviewed) equivalent to AIG-R
Clarified FH as Fully Human (No AI Involvement)
Updated examples and attribution guidance to reference framework versions
compatibility.note: All classifications created using AICCF v1.0 remain valid and unchanged.

attribution.description: Attribution is appreciated when this framework is shared, published, or adapted externally.

final_note: This classification aims to provide a practical and accessible approach to improving transparency, accountability, and trust in AI-assisted work.
